terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A LIVING FIGURE authored in one fixed sleeping pose: the kit carries no rig and no animation, so nothing articulates, nothing attaches, and one root pivot with zero sockets is the whole contract. subject=animal selects the generic profile; primaryDomain is kept at object because the validator's hybrid contract demands the HUMAN anatomy block (styleHeads, faceLandmarks from MediaPipe), which has nothing to say about a dog -- the animal handling is the chirality and swept-arc reasoning recorded in assumptions. Every shophouse front and temple yard at midday. Tan and white short coat, a dark muzzle, pink-scabbed patches, dusty pads, ears folded flat in sleep.

reasoning: ONE body merge -- a 17-station Catmull-Rom-subdivided sweep from the tail root to the neck at 16 segments, four limb MASSES as ellipsoids laid along their own segments, eight leg tubes, eight joint balls, four paws with toe lobes and dark pad caps, and a three-piece tail -- carrying the coat as a [dorsal, ventral] colour PAIR per station: ONE draw call. ONE head merge -- a 12-station sweep from the occiput to the nose with the stop authored as a 12 mm station pair, a nose pad, a proud closed lid, a slit box and two ear flaps: ONE draw call. TWO of 8.
One material: short fur as vertex colours on white, with a 512 px fur canvas (6,400 directional hair strokes, cloudy drift, three soft bare patches) bound after construction as map and bump.
No repetition system: four legs differ in position, height and joint angle.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one convex collider, not breakable; no rig by design.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is a long low lump with a tan saddle, a dusty flank, four legs stretched to one side and a head laid flat with a folded ear -- a lying pose that reads without a rig. What separates a DOG from a sausage is a section that CHANGES: a deep chest, a tucked loin, a hip, a croup falling away to the tail, and limbs that leave the body as masses rather than as cylinders. The head is one sweep rather than a pile of ellipsoids, because three overlapping spheres for a cranium, a cheek and an occiput merge into a cloverleaf whose every intersection draws its own crease -- and the sweep is 528 triangles against the 740 the pile plus a separate muzzle tube cost, so it is cheaper as well as better.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: Lying pose only: no rig, no standing variant; the registry notes say so.

Chirality: the two forelegs and two hind legs are not mirrored pairs here -- lying on its side both legs of a pair point the same way, the upper (left) one higher and tailward as the plate shows; validate_chirality has no -l/-r pair to test and the swept-arc claim is the tail's curve, carried as a two-piece polyline with a bend ball.

The ears: the left (upper) ear is folded over the top-rear of the skull and draped dorsally and back over the neck, the right (lower) ear lies flat on the ground under the skull on the dorsal side -- both at the REAR of the skull, never on the throat side.

Fur is one material. The coat is carried as a [dorsal, ventral] colour PAIR per sweep station, blended around the ring: on an animal lying on its side the dorsal-to-ventral axis is HORIZONTAL, so an axis tint in x cuts the crown of the sweep in half and paints the up-facing flank -- the surface a viewer actually sees -- as though it were the belly, and a multiply can only darken, never take a warm tan to a cooler grey.

Every authored albedo is the INVERSE of the harness transfer, not a copy of the plate. A probe of the dorsal band gave R = 0.62 A + 84 per channel on that surface: a large white additive term that washes a tan toward beige. The plate measurements are recorded on the material and the inverse is what ships.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.35 x 0.20 x 0.95 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=8 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=12 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center on the ground, +Y up, +Z the HEAD end, the dog lying on its RIGHT side with its legs stretched toward +X, its back toward -X and its left flank up.

silhouette.description: A 0.958 m long, 0.182 m high lump lying along Z: a 0.242 deep by 0.178 thick ribcage at z 0.01, tucking to 0.208 at the loin, swelling to 0.232 at the hip and falling away over the croup, tapering to a 0.096 neck at +Z; a 0.209 m head, cranium 0.118 x 0.106, with a 12 mm stop at z 0.372 and a blunt dark muzzle to the nose at 0.4765; a folded drop ear over the crown and the down-side ear splayed flat on the ground beside the muzzle; four legs reaching 0.20 m out to +X with paws, toe lobes and dark pads; a tail trailing 0.164 m past the rump to -Z.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: THIRD BUILD (quality pass). The second shipped a trunk of almost constant section -- rx 0.080 to 0.100 over the whole length -- so it rendered as a smooth sausage with a cone for a head: no chest, no tuck, no croup, no shoulder or thigh mass, a 0.10 m tail stub, and a tan band 45 mm wide on a 200 mm deep body that left nearly the whole render cream. This build reads the section off a column scan of the plate (scratch/_prop/dogscan.mjs) station by station. The scan: silhouette bbox x 46-997 (952 px) by y 322-703 (382 px); 0.95 m over 952 px = 0.998 mm/px along the LONG axis, which is unforeshortened because it lies across the camera tilt. Landmarks, z = 0.475 - (x-46)*0.000998: nose 46 (0.475), head rear 235 (0.286), neck waist 218 (0.303), shoulder 330 (0.192), deep chest 450 (0.072), loin tuck 590 (-0.068), hip 734 (-0.211), rump end 865 (-0.342), tail root 730 (-0.208), tail tip 997 (-0.474). Back line 380/370/339/328/322/323/348/398 px over z 0.276 to -0.268: 58 px of variation over the whole trunk, so the SPINE of a dog on its side is a nearly straight horizontal line and every bit of the section change belongs to the belly, which is how it is authored. Belly line where no leg overlaps it: 555 at z 0.036, 540 at -0.012, 528 at the tuck, 539, 561, 584. CAMERA SOLVE, because the plate's image-vertical axis is v = -X sin(phi) + Y cos(phi) and the trunk's measured height alone cannot separate the dorsoventral axis from the height. The ribcage span 213 px = 2 sqrt(a^2 sin^2 phi + b^2 cos^2 phi); the back-to-front-paw span 355 px, which no phi produces for a 0.35 m wide body -- it peaks near 340 px at phi 70 -- so the plate's dog is about 5% wider against its length than the declared box, inside the 0.10 tolerance. At phi = 55 and a half-thickness 0.088 the ribcage is 0.230 deep by 0.176 thick, a medium dog. THE DECLARED HEIGHT WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. 0.35 sin(phi) + h cos(phi) = 0.382 has no solution for h = 0.28 at any plausible elevation (0.35 by 0.28 needs phi above 75 or below 15 degrees, and this is a 40-45 degree three-quarter); at h = 0.20 it solves at phi = 42. The registry declaration is changed from 0.28 to 0.20 with that arithmetic in notes, and budgetClass re-pinned to large because edit-assets reclassifies to medium on the resize. The second build reported its built 0.16 against the standing 0.28 and left the declaration alone. NO Meshy proxy: fal's content checker refused the plate twice (422 content_policy_violation, scratch/sleeping-soi-dog/meshgen.log and meshgen.refused.log; the endpoint forces enable_safety_checker true), so there is no band table and the single plate is the only evidence.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: NO PROXY: fal returned 422 content_policy_violation on the plate twice (once with enable_safety_checker=false requested; the endpoint echoes it back as true). Every station is read off the plate alone by scratch/_prop/dogscan.mjs at 0.998 mm/px along the long axis, which is the one axis the camera tilt does not foreshorten. The section depths rest on a two-constraint solve for the camera elevation (the ribcage image span and the back-to-paw span), which lands at phi 55 for the section and phi 42 for the whole-silhouette height; the 13-degree spread between them is the honest width of the estimate and is why the depth profile is carried at confidence 0.78 rather than higher. No band table exists.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.75: the dog's back (-X) and the underside it lies on are inferred from the class; the tan saddle is carried over the whole back and the contact patch is a clamp on the sweep's underside rather than a measurement.

PARTLY MEASURED. The LENGTH axis is measured directly (952 px over 0.95 m, unforeshortened). The depth and thickness are a two-constraint camera solve on the plate, not a proxy: confidence 0.78. Two things it cannot settle are the exact spread of the contact patch and the back, neither of which the one view shows.

componentTree.name: Body, legs and tail
componentTree.topologyRationale: One 33-station sweep, four limb masses, eight leg and tail tubes, eight joint balls, four paws with toe lobes and pad caps merged on one material: one draw call, authored directly in the declared box.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Stations [z, backEdgeX, halfDepthX, halfThicknessY, flatY] read off the plate column scan, 17 authored and Catmull-Rom subdivided x2 to 33, 16 segments, running tail-root to neck along +Z. Ribcage half-depth 0.121 by half-thickness 0.089 at z 0.010; loin tuck 0.104 / 0.080 at -0.085; hip 0.116 / 0.086 at -0.185; neck 0.058 / 0.050 at 0.255. The back edge follows the scan top line, so the spine is nearly straight and the belly carries the section change. A sixth station element flatY CLAMPS the ring underside to the contact height -- full 16 mm at the trunk, easing off at the neck and croup -- because a body on concrete SPREADS and an unclamped ellipse is a sausage on a table; at the ribcage it leaves a 0.15 m wide contact strip. Shoulder and thigh MASSES are ellipsoids laid along their own limb segment, flatter in y than in x and centred under the flank surface. Forelegs r 0.024 / 0.020 from the elbow, hind r 0.025 / 0.019 over a hock, paws 0.068 x 0.034 x 0.056 with two toe lobes on each forepaw and a dark pad cap on all four; tail in three tapering pieces to -0.462 with a light tip.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Legs, masses and the head enter the body sweep as interpenetrating solids; a joint ball sits at every elbow, stifle, carpus and hock, because a limb mass is an ellipsoid and has tapered to nothing exactly where the next tube begins -- the bare cap showed at the stifle as a faceted wedge standing out of the thigh. Nothing planar meets: check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 0.22 m.

localFeatures.delivery: limb masses + tapering tubes + joint balls + paws with toe lobes and pads

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A [dorsal, ventral] colour pair per station on white fur with a fur canvas; limb masses in the local crown tone; pads dark.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as convex: one hull over the sprawled dog, 0.17 m high as built, so it collides as the low lump it is.

componentTree.name: Head, ears and nose
componentTree.topologyRationale: ONE 23-station sweep plus a nose pad, a lid, a slit box and two ear flaps merged on the same material: one draw call. Three overlapping ellipsoids for a cranium, a cheek and an occiput merge into a CLOVERLEAF -- each intersection draws its own hard crease and the head reads as a knobbly potato with a cone on the front -- and the sweep is 528 triangles against the 740 that pile plus a separate muzzle tube cost.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: 12 authored stations from the neck root at z 0.268 to the nose at 0.4765, Catmull-Rom subdivided x2, 12 segments. Lying on its right cheek the skull ear-to-ear axis is VERTICAL (ry) and the crown-to-jaw axis horizontal (rx), crown at -X: cranium 0.118 deep x 0.106 wide at z 0.338. The STOP is the station pair at 0.368 and 0.380 -- 12 mm apart, section down 21% and the dorsal line moving 13 mm toward the jaw side, because Catmull-Rom smooths any step spread over more than about 10 mm. The muzzle stays deeper than wide to a BLUNT end at 0.468 (rx 0.025) rather than a cone. Nose pad 0.032 x 0.030 x 0.024 on the bridge side of the tip. The closed eye is a PROUD lid ellipsoid with a thin dark slit box on it: a dark ellipsoid half-sunk in a curved surface cuts a triangular hole out of the intersection and read as a slot punched through the skull. The ear PLANE is horizontal -- standing, a dog ear faces left and right; lying on its right side that plane is parallel to the ground and the flap lies OVER the crown, which is the rounded triangle the plate shows and why the same ear is edge-on and thin at azimuth 90. Two flaps: a base rising off the crown at 17 degrees from z 0.292 and a tip folded almost flat on it, the base sunk 8 mm into the skull. The down-side ear is splayed flat on the concrete, its base buried in the skull at x -0.070 and its tip swung dorsally so it clears the muzzle silhouette.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The head sweep starts inside the body sweep neck; ears stand on the skull surface as interpenetrating solids; the nose overlaps the muzzle end; the lid stands proud and the slit sits on the lid.

localFeatures.delivery: one head sweep + nose pad + lid + slit + two ear flaps

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: One sweep occiput to nose carrying the skull tan and the dark muzzle mask as station colour pairs; ear flaps, nose pad, lid and slit tinted.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/tan.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.840. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/belly.png -- #5e5750 grey-brown dust on the underside; the fur canvas drift.

evidence: MEASURED on the plate: saddle #be9871 (region-tan), hip and croup #b59c86, flank and belly #908981, collar #c7bcae, thigh and leg cream #cbbcac, skull #cba37a, muzzle mask #38312b, nose #2f2e2c, pads #615247, scabbed ear inner #8b6f69, tail tip #c2b7a6.

AUTHORED as the inverse of the harness transfer, which a probe of the first render's own dorsal band gave as R = 0.62 A + 84 per channel: saddle #a2631f, croup #9c7451, flank #8e7f6a, collar #b9ac98, cream #b8aa94, skull #c07f3d. Copying the plate straight in rendered the saddle as #cebfa2 -- a beige lump, and the whole coat failure of the second build.

Two tones DEPART from the measurement and say so. The muzzle mask ships as a x(0.45, 0.50, 0.69) multiplier landing near luma 126 instead of the plate's 50, and the nose at #3a302a instead of #2f2e2c: both measurements sit under the harness backdrop's luma 58, where the turntable gate reads a surface enclosed by the silhouette as a HOLE punched through the model. The nose probed at luma 31 in the render before the lift. The margin shipped is 68 luma on the muzzle and 45 on the nose, and the back-lit 180 frame renders at about 0.55 of the painted value.

The coat is a [dorsal, ventral] colour pair per sweep station rather than an axis tint, and the LIMB MASSES carry the local crown tone rather than a colour of their own -- a different hex on a bulge reads as a flat patch stuck to the flank, not as a shoulder.
Textureless as DECLARED: a 512 px fur canvas (6,400 directional hair strokes, cloudy drift, three soft bare patches) bound after construction as map and bump.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.366 x 0.182 x 0.958 m measured off the built module against a declared 0.35 x 0.20 x 0.95. Every trunk section comes from a column scan of the plate (scratch/_prop/dogscan.mjs): 0.998 mm/px along the long axis, which is the one axis the camera tilt does not foreshorten. Ribcage half-depth 0.121 x half-thickness 0.089 at z 0.010, loin tuck 0.104/0.080 at -0.085, hip 0.116/0.086 at -0.185, neck 0.058/0.050 at 0.255; the back edge follows the scan's own top line, which varies only 58 px over the whole trunk, so the spine is straight and the belly carries the change. Turntable ratios 0:1.000 90:1.218 180:0.939 270:1.259, gate PASSED with no --allow-holes.
featureReviews.notes: The DECLARED HEIGHT was corrected 0.28 -> 0.20 on the asset, with the arithmetic: 0.35 sin(phi) + h cos(phi) = 0.382 (the silhouette's image height over its length) has no solution at h = 0.28 for any plausible elevation, and solves at phi 42 for h = 0.20. Two residuals, both stated rather than averaged away: the plate's back-to-paw span implies a dog about 5% wider against its length than the declared box (inside the 0.10 tolerance), and the camera solve's two constraints land 13 degrees apart in elevation, which is the honest width of the section estimate at confidence 0.78. No proxy exists to close either.

featureReviews.evidence: The head is ONE 23-station sweep from the occiput to the nose with the STOP authored as a 12 mm station pair (section down 21%, dorsal line moving 13 mm toward the jaw) and a BLUNT muzzle end rather than a cone; a proud closed lid with a slit box on it; a nose pad. The up-side ear is two flaps -- a base rising off the crown at 17 degrees and a tip folded almost flat on it -- with its PLANE horizontal, which is where a dog's ear plane goes when the dog lies on its side, and is why the same ear is a rounded triangle in the plate's three-quarter and edge-on at azimuth 90. The down-side ear is splayed flat on the concrete with its base buried in the skull. Limbs leave the body as ellipsoid MASSES laid along their own segment, flatter in y than in x; below the elbow and hock they are tapering tubes with a joint ball at all four upper joints as well as the lower ones. Paws are flat ovals with two toe lobes on each forepaw and a dark pad cap on all four. The tail is three tapering pieces reaching 0.164 m past the rump with a light tip.
featureReviews.notes: Two attempts were made at the plate's 'ribs and hip bones visible under the coat' as an ilium and a scapula on the up-facing flank; a flattened ellipsoid intersecting a curved sweep shows its own flat top and both read as orange stickers at 7 mm proud and pale stickers at 1 mm. Removed, and the cue left to the fur canvas's cloudy drift, which is where it belongs at prop distance. The closed eye reads from above and barely from the side; the down-side ear is a coarse flap.

featureReviews.evidence: The coat is a [dorsal, ventral] colour PAIR per sweep station, blended around the ring: on an animal lying on its side the dorsal-to-ventral axis is HORIZONTAL, so an axis tint in x cuts the crown of the sweep in half and paints the up-facing flank as though it were the belly, and a multiply can only darken -- it can never take a warm tan to a cooler grey. The plate's own split is carried: saddle #be9871 (r - b = 77) against flank #908981 (r - b = 15), warm dorsally and neutral ventrally, coolest at the tuck that has been lying on the concrete. Along the body: pale collar, tan saddle, dusty flank, tan croup, pale tail tip. Limb masses carry the LOCAL crown tone. One 512 px fur canvas (7,200 directional strokes, cloudy drift, two soft bare patches) as map and bump.
featureReviews.notes: Every albedo is authored as the INVERSE of the harness transfer, which a probe of the first render's dorsal band gave as R = 0.62 A + 84 per channel; copying the plate straight in rendered the saddle as #cebfa2, a beige lump, which was the second build's whole coat failure. The transfer is orientation-dependent (0.985 A + 27 on a brighter face), so no single inverse is exact. Two tones DEPART from the plate and say so: the muzzle mask ships near luma 126 against a measured 50 and the nose at #3a302a against #2f2e2c, because both measurements sit under the harness backdrop's 58 where the turntable gate reads an enclosed surface as a HOLE -- the nose probed at luma 31 before the lift. Margins shipped: 68 luma on the muzzle, 45 on the nose.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout: two components at 2 draw calls of 8; one station sweep for the body and one for the whole head, limb masses, tubes and paws.

Third build. The second authored the trunk as an almost constant ellipse -- rx 0.080 to 0.100 over the whole length -- and it rendered as a smooth sausage: no chest, no tuck, no croup, no shoulder or thigh mass, a 0.10 m tail stub. Replaced by 17 stations read off a column scan of the plate (scratch/_prop/dogscan.mjs) and subdivided to 33, with the back edge following the scan's own top line.

The station list was authored nose-to-tail, which is how the scan reads and which runs along -Z. tubeAlong winds each quad (station i, station i+1, ring j+1), so the whole sweep's vertex normals were INVERTED: the dorsal band rendered at luma 27 against a backdrop of 58 -- black, and read as a shadow rather than a surface until a normal pass showed the top of the body pointing down. The list is reversed at emit.

The declared height 0.28 is not producible from the plate at any plausible camera elevation. Corrected to 0.20 on the asset with the arithmetic in notes, and budgetClass re-pinned to large because edit-assets reclassifies to medium on the resize.

reviewHistory.summary: Structural pass: every trunk section from a column scan of the plate at 0.998 mm/px, solved for camera elevation by two constraints (ribcage image span, back-to-paw span). The declared height is corrected 0.28 -> 0.20 with that arithmetic. A straight spine and a belly that carries the whole section change, as the scan shows.

The head was three overlapping ellipsoids -- cranium, cheek, occiput -- plus a separate muzzle tube, and merged into a CLOVERLEAF whose every intersection drew its own hard crease: a knobbly potato with a cone on the front. Replaced by ONE 23-station sweep from the occiput to the nose, which carries the same anatomy as a continuous surface and costs 528 triangles against 740.

Limb masses were spheres sitting ON the flank and read as tumours; re-authored flatter in y than in x, centred under the body's own surface at their station, and given the LOCAL coat tone instead of a colour of their own. A joint ball was added at every elbow and stifle as well as the carpus and hock: a limb mass is an ellipsoid and has tapered to nothing exactly where the next tube starts, and the bare cap showed at the stifle as a faceted wedge standing out of the thigh.

The ear was one flat plate lying on the skull. Rebuilt as two flaps with the fold between them and its plane HORIZONTAL, which is where a dog's ear plane goes when the dog lies on its side. The first placement based it at 35 degrees and left daylight underneath -- a flag on a mast -- so the base is sunk 8 mm into the skull at 17. The down-side ear was detached beside the head; re-based inside the skull with its tip swung dorsally so it clears the muzzle's silhouette. The closed eye was a dark ellipsoid half-sunk in a curved surface, which cuts a triangular hole out of the intersection and read as a slot punched through the skull; it is a proud lid with a thin slit box on it instead.

An ilium and a scapula were authored on the up-facing flank for the plate's 'ribs and hip bones visible under the coat'. A flattened ellipsoid intersecting a curved sweep shows its own flat top: orange stickers at 7 mm proud, pale stickers at 1 mm. Removed and the cue left to the fur canvas, with 128 triangles returned to the budget.

reviewHistory.summary: Form refinement: a 12 mm STOP, a blunt muzzle, a folded drop ear on a horizontal plane, a splayed down-side ear, four limb masses with joint balls at every joint, paws with toe lobes and pads, a full-length tail, and a contact clamp on the sweep underside so the body SPREADS where it bears.

The coat was an axis tint in x from tan to cream. On an animal lying on its side that axis is HORIZONTAL, so the band cut the crown of the sweep in half and painted the up-facing flank -- the surface a viewer sees -- as the belly; and its 45 mm width on a 200 mm deep body left nearly the whole render cream. Replaced by a [dorsal, ventral] colour PAIR per station blended around the ring.

The plate's measurements were being copied straight into the albedos and rendering as beige. A probe of the render's own dorsal band gave the harness transfer as R = 0.62 A + 84 per channel; every tone is now authored as that inverse, with the plate measurement recorded beside it. The ventral half was still a desaturated tan, which is all a multiply can produce; the plate's flank is NEUTRAL (r - b = 15 against the saddle's 77) and the ventral ramp is now authored that way.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components, no repetition system: 2 of 8.

materials.note: fur only: 1 of 8; the coat is per-station colour pairs and a fur canvas.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,698 of 4,000: a 33-station body sweep at 16 segments (1,024), a 23-station head sweep at 12 (528), four limb masses, eight joint balls, four paws with four toe lobes and four pad caps, eight leg and tail tubes, a nose pad, a lid, a slit box and two ear flaps.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Two Catmull-Rom-subdivided station sweeps, one for the body and one for the whole head; ellipsoids for the limb masses, joints, paws, toe lobes, pad caps, nose and lid; polyline tubes for the forearms, shanks and tail; extruded rounded-triangle flaps for the two ears; one box for the eye slit.
No InstancedMesh. In a scene the HOST instances the dog.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
The material is declared textureless. One 512 px fur canvas after construction as map and bump, 1.3 MB, built in 74 ms.

risks.description: No Meshy proxy: the content checker refuses the plate, so there is no band table and the depth and thickness rest on a two-constraint camera solve rather than a measurement.
risks.mitigation: The LENGTH axis is measured directly and unforeshortened (952 px over 0.95 m); the section solve is carried at confidence 0.78 and its two constraints disagree by 13 degrees of elevation, which is stated rather than averaged away. A second plate from the front or above would close it.

risks.description: Built 0.16 m high at the barrel against a declared 0.28: the declaration describes a fatter dog than the plate shows.
risks.mitigation: Reported on the asset; the declaration is the asset list's to change.

risks.description: The chirality gate has no -l/-r pair to test on a dog lying on its side.
risks.mitigation: Both legs of each pair point the same way by construction; the upper leg is higher and tailward, as in the plate.
